spans.s: māla (EI 22), an elevated ground.
Malla (CII 4), a wrestler, a match.
Maladhāri (BL), epithet of a Jain religious teacher.
Mālākāra (LL), a florist. See Mālin.
malla-kara (HRS), found in Nepal inscriptions; tax levied as tribute to the Mallas or for defence against their attack. Cf. turuṣka-daṇḍa, etc. It may also be a professional tax on wrestlers.
malamārgaṇa (LL), cf. Gujarātī mal̤avero; a tax to be utilised when the whole village wants to honour a particular man.
Mālava-gaṇ-āmnāta, Mālava-gaṇa-sthiti, Mālava-pūrvā (EI 23), expressions used in early records in connection with the Vikrama-saṃvat.
Mālavī, dialect of Hindī prevalent in Mālava (Malwa).
Mālavīya (EI 22), ‘the king of Mālava’.
malaya (IA 14), derived from Dravidian malai, ‘a hill’.
Malayāl̤am, name of a language and alphabet.
Maleya-sāhaṇi (Naik's List,
); mentioned alongwith Peyiya-sāhaṇi; official designation. See Sāhaṇi.
Mālima, same as Arabic Mualim, ‘an instructor’ (Ep. Ind., Vol. XXXIV, p. 144).
mallaka (EI 21) a measure.
mallaka-vundhaka, cf. talabhedyā-ghāṇaka-mallaka-vundhaka (IA 18); probably, a professional tax on wrestlers.
Malik, Malika (EI 4; BL), Muslim title of nobility; same as Arabic Malik; also spelt in Indian languages as Mallika.
Mālin (EI 9), a florist. See Mālākāra.
mallāyi-maghamai (SITI), Tamil; probably a customary collection in the market.
malla-nandi-māḍa , probably, ‘māḍa bearing the figure of a wrestler and a bull’, or ‘māḍa minted by Mallanandin’; see māḍa.
malla-māḍa , possibly, ‘māḍa bearing the figure of a wrestler’, or an abbreviation of malla-nandi-māḍa; see māḍa.
